text: No, the 2025 loss is not confirmed as persistent. While the Hansen dataset detected a 13.5-hectare loss in 2025 (4% of the asset), there is no later-year observation to corroborate whether this loss remains ongoing or has been reversed. The JRC 2020 reference confirms 98% of the area was forest in 2020, and the Uruguayan MGAP map (2021) classifies 13.1 hectares as native forest. However, without post-2025 data, we cannot determine if the loss is permanent. The event is validated by the baseline corroboration rule but lacks persistence confirmation.
